modes_discovered: oscillation (rhythmic repetition of any atom: sway, drumming, group nodding)
synchrony (interpersonal mirroring of any atom: mirrored lean, collective inhale, ghost-flicker)
bilateralization (both-sided execution: arm-spread = reach x2 + palm offer)
release/inverse (the undoing of any tension atom: unknotted brow; table names some inverses as atoms, others not)
site-parameterization (tremor@eyelid, brace@knee - several atoms are one primitive at many sites)
notes: HEADLINE: somatic-signals is secretly TWO lists. 46/78 are observable semaphore; 32/78 are interoceptive felt-sense (gut drop, tingling scalp, metallic taste) that no observable atom table can ever cover. The atom table isn't incomplete there - the UNIVERSE is different. A sibling table is demanded: interoceptive-atoms (the pulse surge, the tingle, the heat bloom, the chill, the hollow, the lump, the ache, the vibration, the numbness, the taste phantom, the itch, the dry mouth, the gorge rise).
The atom table + 6 new atoms + 4 modes covers 100% of the observable universe. The experiment converts a fuzzy 'incompleteness' feeling into a sharp boundary claim.

The table secretly wants a generative grammar: ~a dozen primitives (brace, release, open, close, orient, rise, drop, oscillate, contact, expand) x body sites x modes. Jaw clench = brace@jaw; gut brace = brace@viscera. The atoms are the common elements; the grammar is the periodic law behind the table.
Stillness is the vacuum state, not an atom - readable only against expected motion (the unblinking stillness decomposes as gaze lock + freeze with the fear valence subtracted).

Asymmetry found: the table names both poles for some pairs (shoulder rise/drop, flush/blanch, pupil bloom needed its pinch) but only the tension pole for others (brow knit, jaw clench, gut brace lack named releases).
